about.title: Redondo Beach Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription:
Redondo Beach is a compact coastal city of roughly 68,000 people in Los Angeles County, and a lot of daily life here happens on property somebody else controls: storefronts along Artesia Boulevard, parking structures near Aviation Boulevard, apartment walkways, restaurants, and the retail strips that line Route 1 and Inglewood Avenue. When a floor is slick, a handrail is loose, or a walkway is left in disrepair, the person who falls often carries the cost.

California premises liability law asks a specific question in these cases: did the property owner know, or should they reasonably have known, about the hazard and still fail to fix it or warn about it? That idea, called notice, is usually the heart of a Redondo Beach fall claim. Proving it depends on evidence that disappears quickly, including store surveillance footage, incident reports, and photos of the condition before it is cleaned up.

LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects injured residents and visitors with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Redondo Beach Fall Victims Use LawProactive

items.title: Notice is the whole case
items.desc: In California, you generally need to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and did nothing. The attorneys we connect you with know how to pursue maintenance logs, inspection schedules, and prior complaints that establish that knowledge.

items.title: Video does not wait for you
items.desc: Many Redondo Beach businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days. Getting an attorney involved early allows a formal preservation demand to go out before the recording of your fall is gone.

items.title: Deadlines vary by who owns the property
items.desc: Most premises claims carry a two-year filing deadline, but a fall on city, county, or state property triggers a much shorter government claim window. An attorney can sort out ownership quickly so the clock does not run out on you.

items.question: I slipped on a public sidewalk in Redondo Beach. Is that different from falling in a store?
items.answer: Yes, and the difference matters. If the property is owned or maintained by the City of Redondo Beach, Los Angeles County, or the State, you generally must file a government claim within six months of the injury before any lawsuit is possible. That is far shorter than the two-year deadline for a private business, so identifying the responsible entity early is essential.

items.question: The store says I was not watching where I was going. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: No. California follows pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by whatever share of responsibility is assigned to you, not eliminated. A property owner who left a hazard in place still carries their portion of the blame, and an attorney can push back on efforts to shift all of it onto you.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall on someone else's property?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if you feel embarrassed or think it is minor, because fall injuries often worsen over the next day or two. If you are able, photograph the exact spot, the hazard, your footwear, and any missing warning signs, and ask that an incident report be written. Then request that any surveillance video be preserved, and reach out so we can connect you with an attorney who can make that request formally.
